passage: 14 March Did it. Finally went to Jaya ma'am's office hours and said the words: "I have dyslexia. Could I get the reading list early, and extra time in the mid-sems?" My voice was shaking and I stared at her plant the whole time. I'd practised it for a week. She just nodded and said, "Of course. Thank you for telling me. Would audio versions help?" That's it. No face. No sigh. All this semester I've been listening to the chapters on my phone at double speed on the bus and dictating notes with the voice tool. I thought using them was cheating. It isn't. It's how I read. Got back my essay today too: "Sharp argument." Pinned it above the desk. - Santosh

qa.a: Santosh told the tutor about the dyslexia and asked for support, and was met with understanding and an offer of audio versions.

qa.q: How does Jaya ma'am seem to see Santosh's request?
qa.a: She treats it as normal and reasonable, even thanking Santosh for telling her.

grounding: It shows a young adult who uses audio and voice tools, feels embarrassed to ask for extra time, and is met with understanding when sharing the difference.
